## Hypothesis

H1: Points allocated to a partner's physical attractiveness differ by sex at birth.

H2: Confidence in finding a new partner is associated with relationship commitment.

```{r load package}
library(ggplot2)
library(ggrain)
```

## Load the processed data

```{r loadData}
#load processed data
h1Data <- read.csv("data/processed_data/practice_h1.csv")
h2Data <- read.csv("data/processed_data/practice_h2.csv")

#reorganize categorical variable
h1Data$Sex_birth <- factor(h1Data$Sex_birth,
                           levels=c("Male","Female","Intersex"))

```

## H1 - Box Plot

```{r H1Box}
#Box plot
#The line is the median; the box covers the middle 50% of responses (Q1-Q3).
#Whiskers reach the most extreme observations within 1.5 IQR of the box edges.
#Points beyond the whiskers are not necessarily errors.
h1Box <- ggplot(data=h1Data,
                aes(x=Sex_birth,
                    y=preference_imp_physat,
                    fill=Sex_birth)) +
  geom_boxplot()+
  labs(x="Sex assigned at birth",
       y="Points allocated to partner attractiveness",
       fill="Sex at birth",
       title="Allocation to partner attractiveness by sex")+
  theme_gray(base_size=15)

h1Box

```

## H1 - Violin Plot (with Box Plot)

```{r H1Violin}
#Violin Plot
#Wider sections show where responses are more concentrated within each group.
#The shape depends on smoothing; integer scores can create bumps.
#Violin width does not show group sample size. The box adds the median and IQR.
h1Viol <- ggplot(data=h1Data,
                 aes(x=Sex_birth,
                    y=preference_imp_physat,
                    fill=Sex_birth))+
  geom_violin()+
  geom_boxplot(width=.12)+
labs(x="Sex assigned at birth",
       y="Points allocated to partner attractiveness",
       fill="Sex at birth",
       title="Allocation to partner attractiveness by sex")+
  theme_gray(base_size=15)

h1Viol

```

## H1 - Raincloud Plot

```{r H1Raincloud}
#Raincloud Plot
#A raincloud combines a half-violin, a box plot, and individual responses.
#Jitter separates overlapping points without changing the recorded values.
#With many responses, points can still overlap heavily.
h1Rain <- ggplot(data=h1Data,
                 aes(x=Sex_birth,
                    y=preference_imp_physat,
                    fill=Sex_birth))+
  geom_rain(alpha = .5)+
  labs(x="Sex assigned at birth",
       y="Points allocated to partner attractiveness",
       fill="Sex at birth",
       title="Allocation to partner attractiveness by sex")+
  theme_gray(base_size=15)

h1Rain
  
```

## H2 - Scatter Plots

```{r H2Scatter}
#Scatter Plot
h2Points <- ggplot(data=h2Data,
                    aes(x=qoa,
                        y=commitment))+
  geom_point()+
  labs(x="Confidence in finding a new partner",
       y="Relationship commitment",
       title="Confidence in finding a new partner and commitment")+
  theme_gray(base_size = 18)

h2Points

#Plot looks weird... why?
nrow(h2Data)
nrow(unique(h2Data[,c("qoa","commitment")]))

#Jitter
h2Jitter <- ggplot(
  data=h2Data,
                    aes(x=qoa,
                        y=commitment))+
    geom_jitter(width = .12,height=.04,alpha=.04,size = .6)+
    labs(x="Confidence in finding a new partner",
       y="Relationship commitment",
       title="Confidence in finding a new partner and commitment")+
  theme_gray(base_size = 18)


h2Jitter

```

## H2 - Smooth Line

```{r}
#Scatter Plot with line
h2Line <- h2Jitter + geom_smooth(method="lm")

h2Line

```

## Save figures

```{r saveFigures}
#Run after creating the plots. Save PNG files in the project's figures folder.
dir.create("figures",showWarnings=FALSE)
ggsave("figures/h1_raincloud.png",plot=h1Rain,width=10,height=6,dpi=300)
ggsave("figures/h2_scatter.png",plot=h2Line,width=10,height=6,dpi=300)
#To save another plot, change the filename and plot object (e.g., h1Viol or h1Rain).
```

## Other graphs - Cheat sheet (TA only)

### Mean bar graph with confidence intervals

Based on Prediction 1.1 in the course cheat script. Use this to compare group
means; the bars do not show the distribution of individual responses.

```{r meanBar}
#Bar height shows the mean; error bars show bootstrap 95% confidence intervals.
#mean_cl_boot requires Hmisc; install it once in the Console if needed.
#These intervals resample individuals and do not account for clustering by country.
set.seed(221)

h1Mean <- ggplot(data=h1Data,
                 aes(x=Sex_birth,
                     y=preference_imp_physat,
                     fill=Sex_birth))+
  stat_summary(fun="mean",geom="bar")+
  stat_summary(fun.data="mean_cl_boot",geom="errorbar",width=.15)+
  labs(x="Sex assigned at birth",
       y="Mean points allocated to partner attractiveness",
       fill="Sex at birth")

h1Mean
```

### Count bar graph

An additional example. Use this to check how many respondents are in each
category, rather than comparing their mean scores.

```{r countBar}
#geom_bar counts rows in each category; no y variable is needed.
h1Count <- ggplot(data=h1Data,
                  aes(x=Sex_birth,fill=Sex_birth))+
  geom_bar()+
  labs(x="Sex assigned at birth",
       y="Number of respondents",
       fill="Sex at birth")

h1Count
```

### Histogram

An additional example. Use this to inspect the distribution of one numeric
variable. Unlike a violin, it displays counts in bins without smoothing.

```{r histogram}
#binwidth=1 creates one-point intervals; center=0 centers bins on whole numbers.
#Changing the bin width changes the detail visible in the distribution.
h1Hist <- ggplot(data=h1Data,aes(x=preference_imp_physat))+
  geom_histogram(binwidth=1,center=0,color="white")+
  labs(x="Points allocated to partner attractiveness",
       y="Number of respondents")

h1Hist

#Show each group in its own panel using the same axes.
#These are counts, so larger groups will have taller bars.
h1Hist + facet_wrap(~Sex_birth)
```
